About this item

  • 【Wall Mounted Requirements】 Concrete wall or brick wall is suggested for mounting this pull up bar and dip station. DON'T install on drywall, plaster walls and cavity.
  • 【Heavy Duty Steel Construction】 This wall mounted pull up bar is made of heavy duty steel,which offers great stability and rigidity,supports up to 440 pounds.
  • 【Multifunctional】Can be used for a variety of exercises that effectively build muscle across the chest, arms, back and core with chin-ups, push-ups, dip station,leg raises.
  • 【Comfortable,Durable Cushion】Tear resistant,Well-padded,high density,padded back and arm cushions provide comfort as you work out your abdomen, waist, chest, and upper limbs.
  • 【Easy to Assemble】4 (7mm) Strong Suspension Anchors. For assembly and installation you will need: Hammer drill with 12mm(15/32 In) for concrete or brick walls.

How customer reviews and ratings work

Customer Reviews, including Product Star Ratings help customers to learn more about the product and decide whether it is the right product for them.

To calculate the overall star rating and percentage breakdown by star, we don’t use a simple average. Instead, our system considers things like how recent a review is and if the reviewer bought the item on Amazon. It also analyzed reviews to verify trustworthiness.

Customers say

Customers find the pull-up bar sturdy and functional, with one mentioning it works well with TRX and another noting it pairs excellently with an Intense Band for pull-ups. They appreciate its versatility for multiple exercises and consider it well worth the purchase price. While some customers report it holds up to 220lbs without issues, others mention it tilts to one side. The durability receives mixed feedback, with customers reporting it holds up well after two months of use, though one customer mentions a weld coming apart. The wall mounting system also receives mixed reviews, with one customer noting it comes with serious iron hooks for installation.

Heavy Duty Legit Multifunctional Pull Up Bar
This is my first product review on Amazon - love this multifunctional pull-up bar. It’s heavy duty legit and comes with serious iron hooks for wall mounting. We put it in our garage, which has drywall. To secure the hooks to the studs, I bought lag bolts and washers. Also I’m a design nerd and anal, so I built a small 1x4 frame and painted it to match the bar. It’s super secure and looks good too!

    Quality build, versatile grips, and excellent comfort
    Reviewed in the United States on June 22, 2025
    Color: Red
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I installed the ONETWOFIT wall pull‑up & dip station about two weeks ago, and it’s been excellent. Setup took about an hour using my stud-finder and drill. The steel frame feels solid—no wobble even during heavy kips. I love the multiple grip options, which make targeting different back and arm muscles easy. The dip handles are an unexpected bonus and feel stable.

    The padded grips are soft but firm, preventing calluses. The unit doesn’t jut out too much.

    Pros:

    • Versatile: Pull‑ups, dips, leg raises, and more in one unit.

    • Plug‑and‑play: Includes all mounting hardware.

    • Great price: High-end functionality without breaking the bank.

    Cons:

    • Wall drilling: You need solid studs.

    • Width: Takes about 40″ of wall space.

    Bottom line: If you want a single wall-mounted station for full upper‑body workouts, this is it. Quality build, versatile grips, and excellent comfort—all at a reasonable price.

    This wondrous creation, fashioned to withstand the burdens of Herculean endeavors, boasts a stout capacity of support, offering succor to those of brawn and sinew up to 440 pounds. Lo, the mightiest of men and women shall find solace in its sturdy embrace, as it permits the execution of a myriad of exercises, propelling the body to ascend to the pinnacle of strength and grace.

    Mounted upon the walls of one's dwelling, it doth not encroach upon the precious expanse of the homely abode, for it is a guardian of space. The wretched limitations of square footage shan't deter the intrepid seeker of fitness, for this pull-up bar, chin-up bar, and dip station hath been designed with ingenuity to save the precious resource of room.

    Engage in the primal ritual of the pull-up, with hands gripping the bar in resolute determination, as muscles strain and sinews tremble. Ascend with each mighty exertion, as the very fibers of thy being undergo transformation. A dip station awaits, ready to accommodate thy body's descent, as thou challengest the might of gravity and sculpt thy triceps with a fierce resolve.

    O, how this multifunctional contrivance bestows upon its master the gifts of strength, endurance, and the radiant glow of accomplishment! Verily, the path to physical prowess lies within the grasp of this apparatus, and those who dare to seize it shall be rewarded.

    Let praises resound, let the voices of accolade be heard, for the OneTwoFit Multifunctional Wall Mounted Pull Up Bar Chin Up bar Dip Station is a testament to the wonders of invention. In the realm of fitness and the pursuit of bodily excellence, it doth reign supreme.

    Reviewed in the United States on November 29, 2020
    Color: Red
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Wroks as advertised. The hooks for the lower wall position to allow dips must be set to a narrower width than the top postiion or else the leg lift arm rests will hit the lower hooks. Unlike the top hooks, the lower narrower position for the hooks will not align with 16" space wall studs so you need to mount into wood or something else as others have posted. A more thoughtful design could eliminate this problem so this is why i'm only giving 4 stars. If the wall is drywall you definitely want to mount into wood anyway as you need to protect the drywall as switching positions will mark up the wall. I put plywood over the drywall and mounted into studs, keeping both top and bottom hooks the same width. I then angled the leg lift arm pads so they don't hit the lower hooks when the rack is in the top position. Not perfect but it works and I feel better knowing both sets of hooks are into studs.

    So with COVID I canceled my gym membership and opted to workout at home. The problem was space. I had been looking for something like this unit for a while and after reading the reviews I bought it. Best thing I ever did. The chin ups, wide grip and close, are great. The ability to convert it into a dip station/ab workout station really put this product over the edge as far as it’s multi function use. Between this purchase and the Nordic Trak adjustable weight dumbells and bench, I have everything I need in a very compact space. The ONLY issue I have with this is that I spent $50 in lag bolts, washers and a 2x8 (cut into 4-24” sections for mounting to studs) for installation. So figure this into the cost of this unit because it only comes with bolts for installation on a concrete wall. Find your studs for mounting and you will be good to go. I read one review that stated the unit had some flex. I used a couple of rubber washers where the chin up bar attaches to the unit as there was a gap and this fixed it. This may sound like a lot of extra work for the build and install, however the unit is 100% worth it. Very sturdy. Again... Game Changer for a home gym.

    5 out of 5 stars
    Space Saving and Solid!
    Reviewed in the United States on March 24, 2025
    Color: Red
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I bought this to replace a self-standing exercise tower to save some space in my home gym. Following what others here have said, I ended up purchasing some 1x6 wood and 3.5 inch lag bolts for the hooks. The lags go through the 1x6 into studs so the wood is really only there for added support and to protect the wall. I've seen different methods in other reviews but this seemed like the most straightforward way with minimum materials. As long as your studs are 16 inches on center then the hooks should have enough space to hold the inside of the frame while the bumpers come to rest just an inch or two left and right of where the hooks are mounted.

    Assembly was pretty easy with the included tools. Just pay close attention to screw lengths as they aren't all the same. You'll mostly rely on diagrams and labels so sort the hardware into groups first so you don't mix up screws "1", "2", and "3".

    It feels very sturdy compared to the old standalone tower and I'm loving it so far! The unit itself is not that heavy and easy to switch between the two hanging positions. I weigh about 190 and I hardly feel it flex, even when doing dips.

    Installation took a bit of work, but I’m happy with how it turned out
    Reviewed in the United States on January 21, 2026
    Color: Red
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Not the most straightforward drywall install, but I’m very happy with the final result and it saves a ton of space in my home gym. I picked up a 48×24" sheet of pre-finished plywood (cut down to 42" on the vertical side) along with all the necessary hardware for stud mounting (5/16" lag screws and a box of #9 decking screws).

    I do wish they included a wall template similar to what you get with TV mounts, but I was able to rig up a cardboard cutout that helped me dial in the exact placement. Before drilling, it’s helpful to mark all the studs with painter’s tape and line everything up with the plywood backing.

  • James D
    5 out of 5 stars
    Nice unit. Some install tricks.
    Reviewed in Canada on May 25, 2020
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    This unit is quite sturdy. I’m about 230lbs and this bar setup feels very secure and stable.

    Note that the bar must be installed on a concrete wall or you’ll have to get creative. It cannot be installed on a plain drywall wall.

    For my installation I added a 3/4” sheet of plywood and bolted through that To attach the hooks with 3/8” bolts and fat washers. I then fastened the plywood securely to three wall studs using 2.5” 1/4” lag bolts and washers. I used 18 of them. Overkill? Maybe. But this thing is not going anywhere.

    Assembly of the bar is pretty straightforward but the instructions are not great. I did have to take it apart a bit in order to flip a couple things around but it’s simple to look at the photos and figure it out.

    One warning though. The tube metal is not super thick. I was using a socket wrench to tighten things down and it appears it’s pretty easy to over tighten things and stat collapsing the tubing. Just be careful and there’s no probs.

    Pros:

    Wall-mounted for space-saving and solid stability

    Supports up to 440 lbs, suitable for most users

    Easy to install with clear instructions and hardware included

    Great for a variety of workouts—pull-ups, dips, leg raises, and more

    Cons:

    Requires a sturdy wall for secure mounting

    Installation takes some time and effort, best with two people

    Personal Experience:

    I installed this in my garage gym, and it’s been fantastic for strengthening my arms, shoulders, and core. The padded grips are comfortable even during longer sets, and the unit feels rock-solid once mounted. Having the dip station built-in is a huge bonus—it’s rare to find all these features in one compact setup. Just make sure you mount it securely!

    Verdict:

    For anyone looking to build upper body and core strength at home without taking up too much space, the ONETWOFIT wall-mounted pull-up and dip station is a versatile and reliable choice. It offers excellent stability, comfort, and functionality for serious training.
